sentences.text: ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL) Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and perused the record.

2. The present is a wholly misconceived petition filed with a prayer to seek mandamus commanding the respondent no. 2, namely the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Ahmedabad to refer the application preferred by the petitioner under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 to the Rajnikant Jayantibhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98563402/
1 concerned Court within stipulated time frame.

sentences.text:
In order to seek the above noted directions, it is sought to be submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that on declaration of the award dated 10.10.2006 in LAQ Case No. 5 of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/92/2025 ORDER DATED:
07/01/2025 undefined 2004, the petitioner being dissatisfied with the market value/ quantum of compensation along with other heirs of deceased Jayantibhai Naranbhai Patel, had preferred an application dated 09.11.2006 to refer the matter to the Court under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1894").
2.1.

It is further submitted that on receipt of the said application, vide communication dated 13.12.2006, the competent authority had requested the learned advocate for the petitioner to provide certain details/documents.

It is contended in paragraph '4' of the writ petition that the petitioner immediately complied with the letter dated 13.12.2006 and provided necessary details in the form of an undertaking which is appended as Annexure-'D' to the writ petition.

It is further stated in paragraph '4' of the writ petition that the original undertaking supplied to respondent no. 2 contains the date and signature of the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner and the document appended as Annexure-'D' is office copy of the same, wherein the date of undertaking and signature have not been incorporated.
2.2.

The further statement in paragraph '5' of the writ petition is that the petitioner thereafter regularly visited the office of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/92/2025 ORDER DATED:
07/01/2025 undefined respondent no. 2 in the year 2007 and requested to send the reference to the competent Civil Court.

The petitioner has submitted that he remained under the impression that the reference has been forwarded to the Civil Court, however, in the year 2023, when the land acquisition reference of other land holders came up for hearing, the petitioner inquired from the office of respondent no. 2 and it was learnt at that point of time that the reference of the petitioner was not forwarded to the Civil Court.
The representations were, thereafter, filed by the petitioner in the months of January, February, May and July, 2024.
2.3. It is contended that vide letter dated 24.07.2024, it was intimated by respondent no. 2 that the reference application filed by the petitioner could not be traced in its office.

Thereafter, the petitioner filed documents to respondent no. 2 along with the communication dated 03.08.2024,
which included copy of application preferred by the petitioner on 09.11.2006 under Section 18 of the Act, 1894; copy of the letter dated 13.12.2006; copy of the award dated 10.10.2006 and copy of the letter dated 24.07.2024.

It is further contended that vide letter dated 24.09.2024, the respondent no. 2 had informed that the compliance as sought from the petitioner had not been done and at that moment, the petitioner was NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/92/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/01/2025 undefined constrained to approach this Court.

The present petition therefore, has been filed for inaction of the respondent no. 2 in not making a reference for a period of more than 17 years inspite of the completion of the formalities by the petitioner.
3. Taking note of the above stand of the petitioner in the writ petition, we have perused the communication dated 13.12.2006 at page '41' of the paper book.
We may note that the application dated 13.12.2006 was filed by the petitioner herein along with other claimants seeking for reference of the dispute under Section 18 of the Act, 1894.

The copy of the alleged application dated Rajnikant Jayantibhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98563402/
2 09.11.2006 appended at page '37' of the paper book indicates that it was submitted in the matter of award passed in LAQ Case No. 5 of 2004.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that there is a reference of an application under Section 18 of the Act, 1894 moved by the petitioner on 09.11.2006 in the communication dated 13.12.2006 which was addressed to the Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner before the respondent no. 2.
The said communication categorically records that there were discrepancies in the application moved by the petitioner and fresh application was required to be moved after removal of defects.

The objections were taken in the communication dated 13.12.2006 with regard to the description of the land in NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/92/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/01/2025 undefined question, the name of the tenure holders and the lack of complete information in the application under Section 18 of the Act, 1894.
There is no dispute about the fact that the communication dated 13.12.2006 was received by the petitioner.

The assertion of the petitioner that by giving undertaking immediately on receipt of the communication dated 13.12.2006 appended at page '42' of the paper book (Annexure-'D'), the petitioner had completed all formalities of making of reference and the defects have been removed.

The undertaking at page '42'
of the paper book is undated and unsigned document and that too the said undertaking only refers to the court fee which has not been paid in view of the decision of this Court.
The said undertaking indicates that the claimants undertake to pay the court fee to the Government or the Court if it is ordered.

4. We may also note that there is nothing on record to establish that the undertaking which is an unsigned undated document appended at page '42' of the paper book was duly submitted in the office of respondent no. 2.

There is no application or covering letter to indicate that the defects as pointed out in the communication dated 13.12.2006 sent by the learned advocate on behalf of the petitioner were removed within a reasonable time.

5. Be that as it may, from the own assertion of the petitioner in NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/92/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/01/2025 undefined the writ petition, he remained silent till the year 2024 when for the first time the representation dated 02.01.2024 was sent by the petitioner asking the respondent no. 2 to make a reference.
The respondent no

. 2 in the letter dated 24.07.2024 has clearly communicated to the petitioner that the application allegedly filed under Section 18 of the Act, 1894 could not be traced in the office of the respondent no.2.
The said communication also requires the petitioner to give proof of the documents of the submission of the compliance to the communication dated 13.12.2006.

There is a complete silence in the writ petition about any step taken by the petitioner in the interregnum i.e. after 13.12.2006 till 02.01.2024 when for the first time the representation has been filed on the premise that the application under Section 18 of the Act, 1894 was duly moved by the petitioner and the matter has not been referred to the competent Civil Court.
There is no explanation whatsoever, for the inordinate laches of 18 years on the part of the petitioner.

Moreover, as per the response given by the respondent no. 2, the application under Section 18 of the Act, 1894 is not traceable in the office of respondent no. 2 and the petitioner has failed to submit any proof of filing the same after receipt of the communication dated 13.12.2006 from the office of the respondent no. 2, we do not find it a fit case to interfere.
